what: controls that read Python source as TEXT, one row per (file, function)
why_this_count: 187 -> 352 on 2026-09-09, when taint began crossing a call boundary within a module. The 165 are not new controls and not a regression: they are what the per-scope rule could never see, and the old floor was a floor over the visible half. 2 rows went the other way, where a module's own ast.parse helper now reads as the parse it is. 355 -> 361 on 2026-09-09: the six added are all `tools/promoted_artefact_claim_census.py` and NOT six new scanners. One nested closure moved out of `_artefact_dates` into `_tokens_anywhere_in` when run-identity grading stopped guessing and started reading the producer's declaration, and taint that used to terminate inside that closure now crosses the call. The module's one real source-as-text reader, `_module_strings`, already goes through `ast` and `tokenize`; the rest are dismissals over a JSON payload or a container-membership test. Added by hand, not by `--freeze`, which would have rewritten every other lane's rows from a dirty tree. A SEVENTH row on the same day, and `--check` could not see it: the census reads `git ls-files`, so the new test module was invisible while untracked and only the commit gate -- which runs against the tree the commit creates -- reported it. The row is a dismissal: that test walks JSON payloads on disk and splits dotted field paths; the module's Python-source legs go through `ast.parse` and are correctly not flagged.
a_row_is_not_a_verdict: most rows outside tests/ are dismissals carrying a reason -- a non-Python subject, a container-membership test, or a widening prefilter whose verdict comes from a parse tree. The floor bounds GROWTH; read the row before routing it.
how_to_shrink: route the scan through tools/python_code_text.py, then delete its row
